## Processes and privileges

The API validates bearer credentials before every surface, including docs and
health. Consumer and operator tokens must differ. Only the operator token can
submit jobs or read their output through `/operations`; it also works for normal
queries. This is a single-operator credential model, not a multi-user account store.
Neo4j Community Edition users have equivalent database privilege, so application
user naming is credential hygiene rather than database role isolation.

The API writes a bounded SQLite queue on a local named volume. One worker takes a
lifetime file lock, claims jobs transactionally, and invokes only the validated
command allowlist as argv with no shell. Pending capacity is 256; output retains
the last 32 KiB; default operation timeout is 24 hours, configurable up to 7 days.
Request UUIDs provide idempotent submission. Duplicate UUIDs with different payloads
fail with 409. Interrupted running jobs become failed on recovery and are never
automatically repeated; inspect recorded ingestion/model results before retrying.
Queued jobs survive restarts. SQLite volumes require local storage with working
POSIX locks; network filesystems and multiple hosts are outside this topology.

All service processes run as UID/GID 7474, drop Linux capabilities, and disallow
new privileges. Neo4j owns its data and dump processes; the worker owns archive
content, job execution and model pins. Both share the same non-root UID to access
archive files. Configuration binds are read-only; model pins and evaluation data
have writable named volumes seeded by the images. The API mounts the models and
source archive volumes read-only. Authenticated
assertion evidence reads decompress at most 64 KiB for previews; missing or truncated
archives are explicit. These previews do not fetch external sources.
The images contain their ontology, prompts, gold set and reference questions.

## Physical backup and lifecycle

The Neo4j image contains a small supervisor, replacing the inline Compose wrapper.
It starts the stock Neo4j entrypoint, checks admin readiness, validates the app-user
identifier and provisions it idempotently, then checks app-user readiness. Signals
are forwarded to the database process group; a crashed child fails the container.
The private port 9001 accepts only one fixed POST `/backup`, protected by its own
backup token. It is never published to the host. The worker holds that token and
uses this action when processing an operator backup job.

Backup serializes requests, sends SIGTERM to Neo4j, requires clean exit within
180 seconds, invokes `neo4j-admin database dump` offline, rejects empty dumps,
renames the dump with UTC timestamp and random suffix, restarts in a finally block,
and verifies readiness before success. No SIGKILL is followed by a dump. Failed
stop/dump/recovery is a failed job. The graph is unavailable during backup; the
API and durable queue remain up. Dump files and content-addressed source archive
share the archive volume. A database dump alone does not back up the source archive,
model pins, queue or operator configuration; preserve those volumes/files too.

## Surviving graph contracts

Ontology drives entity/relation types and consumer schema. Assertions retain
validity and recorded time independently and preserve contradictions. Empty
results include hop-level coverage/diagnosis. Content-addressed archive remains
the system of record. Parse validation and read-mode driver sessions remain two
independent barriers to writes through query endpoints. Infrastructure construction
remains in composition.py with the documented API startup exception.

G1 now pins API-only loopback publication; G2 pins absent Dash; G3 keeps spaCy
worker-only; G4 removes budget gates. The old exact-three-writes claim applies to
query graph writes, not the dedicated bounded operator queue. Non-root identity,
no socket/control privilege, separate operator auth, and backup clean stop are
additional tested invariants. Routine model/prompt changes need normal review,
cache/provenance version keys and meaningful tests, without budget ceremonies.

## News ingestion: current behavior and accepted target

The worker already has structured source adapters, curated per-entry RSS/Atom
documents, shared extraction and entity resolution, ontology validation/loading,
and Neo4j-native entity vectors. Assertions preserve bitemporal provenance.
Current extraction cannot explicitly represent attribution, denial, modality or
event lifecycle; Event declares only label, source_event_id and occurred_at.

BE-42 decodes bounded official 61-column ZIP/TSV exports and loads coded
observations independently of document gating/cache. Row-scoped provenance
retains archive hash, ZIP member, row, event ID, export/report URLs and DATEADDED;
SQLDATE remains event validity, fetch time remains recorded time. FIPS country
codes are converted explicitly. The API exposes missing article text; exports
are never fabricated into documents. Only SOURCEURL report associations are
covered; Mentions and article retrieval remain future acquisition work.
See [VERIFICATION](VERIFICATION.md) for candidate evidence and its limits.

The accepted target is integrated news intelligence inside the existing worker,
archive, resolver, ontology, loader, API and desktop. Preserve independent coded
observations and source documents, dispatch versions and evidence spans, attributed
claims versus facts, non-destructive event matching and source dependence. No
standalone extractor/utility, event-ledger application, extra service or vector
store is planned. [core design](LIMES_Design_Document_v2.0.0.md) defines the target
contracts; [ROADMAP](ROADMAP.md) orders complete repair, extraction and analysis
packages with prerequisites and acceptance. BE-42 repairs ingestion next;
BE-43/DC-15 adds dynamic investigation-driven news and qualified claim artifacts;
BE-44/DC-16 owns subsequent cross-source analysis.
BE-41 reconciles the documentation baseline. These target contracts do not alter
the shipped runtime table or relax current extraction safeguards.

## Entity and company enrichment: BE-46

`wikipedia` and `yahoo_finance` are registered selection-only sources. Submit
bounded `enrich` operator jobs with reviewed entity/QID/listing mappings; bulk
ingest never implicitly selects companies. Reads make no provider requests.

Wikipedia retains original DE/EN revision responses and wikitext context, page/
revision IDs, timestamps, contributor attribution, history and CC BY-SA 4.0 links.
Context exists without extraction. Optional context extraction uses shared
prompt/schema 2.0.0, cache/resolver and qualified claims with exact revision spans.
A page QID mismatch, ambiguity, redirect or missing sitelink stays explicit.

Yahoo uses pinned yfinance 1.7.0 with bounded response buffering, rate/backoff and
private transient cookie storage. Separate sections preserve profile/officer
observations, named holdings, aggregate ratios, earnings calendars and supplied
filings. Unknown currency/basis/term/report dates stay unknown. Officers do not
establish a complete board; estimates are not published reports. Overlapping
holders and multiple listings are never summed into a cap table.

Ontology 1.2.0 adds immutable EnrichmentSnapshot/EnrichmentObservation and distinct
Security/SecurityListing artifacts with four connecting relations. Declared typed
properties reach graph/entity/builder APIs without overwriting registry history.
Reviewed QID mappings reuse registry company identities; holder/officer names
produce unresolved candidates. No snapshot disappearance causes a retraction.
EnrichmentCheck records acquisition attempts independently from immutable versions.
Authenticated `/entity/{entity_id}/enrichment` reads expose source/section status,
source dates, acquisition checks, freshness basis, evidence and bounded history.
Existing desktop entity/evidence views consume these artifacts through HTTP.

Trust ranks are Wikipedia 0.65 and Yahoo Finance 0.70. Source-format evidence and
access/retention review are in tests/fixtures/enrichment/README.md; these are
secondary incomplete sources, with no commercial redistribution or production
qualification inferred. German and European policy remains the scope.
